comparison: Both strongly support the primary therapeutic finding (C4-C6, C33-C34, C105-C106). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and converging evidence lines. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'convincing data' and 'compelling,' with acknowledgment that hypoglycemia was mitigated (C117). High agreement on this core finding.

Perfect agreement on claims C35-C37, C39, C108 regarding blood gas measurements and acidosis improvements. Both evaluations support these findings without challenge. OpenEval notes the glycolytic inference is reasonable despite lack of direct flux measurement; peer reviewers accept the data without raising concerns.

Significant disagreement on bacterial density findings (C42). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment that mechanism wasn't investigated. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting the possibilities (immune clearance vs. slower bacterial growth) are 'not fully disentangled,' indicating this is a weakness requiring resolution.

OpenEval supports hematology/cellular response claims (C44-C46) while acknowledging mechanism uncertainty. Peer reviewers support the inflammatory findings (C44-C46, C48-C49) as 'compelling' without raising concerns about the cellular response data. Partial overlap with general agreement on inflammatory attenuation.

Major disagreement on hepatic transcriptomic interpretation (C7, C52-C57, C109, C113). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong evidence for metabolic reprogramming. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether changes are 'due to bacterial load rather than metabolic reprograming from the low glucose PN,' challenging the causal mechanism.

Both rate gluconeogenesis claims (C8, C65-C67, C114, C119) as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes lack of direct flux measurement. Peer Reviewer 2 directly challenges the gene expression interpretation, pointing out that PGM2 and GCK patterns contradict the authors' claims, suggesting genes are 'getting upregulated by infection' rather than supporting enhanced gluconeogenesis. Strong agreement on uncertainty, with peer review providing more critical analysis.

Disagreement on systemic anti-inflammatory effects (C9-C10, C48-C49, C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with convergent evidence from cytokines and transcriptomics. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether inflammatory dampening is 'due to bacterial load rather than metabolic reprograming,' suggesting it may be secondary rather than direct effect.

Overlapping claims on inflammatory markers (C48-C49). OpenEval supports the anti-inflammatory interpretation. Peer reviewers accept inflammatory findings as 'compelling' and well-demonstrated. Agreement on the data quality, though peer review raises mechanism questions elsewhere.

Both support metabolomic findings (C60-C64, with overlap on C63-C64). OpenEval emphasizes PCA separation and TCA cycle elevation supporting glycolytic interpretation. Peer reviewers accept these metabolomic data without challenge, treating them as part of the 'impressive' multiomics dataset. Strong agreement.

Both support the hepatic vs. blood metabolic distinction (C68-C76, C110-C111, C115-C116). OpenEval notes striking tissue differences and acknowledges whole tissue limitations. Peer reviewers accept this as a novel insight without challenge, treating the multiomics data as 'impressive.' Strong agreement on this key mechanistic finding.

Both support proteomic findings (C77-C82). OpenEval emphasizes temporal progression and glucose-driven glycolytic protein elevation. Peer reviewers accept these data as part of the comprehensive multiomics dataset without raising concerns. Agreement on data quality and interpretation.

Both support IAIP proteomic findings (C83-C84). OpenEval notes differential regulation by glucose supply. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge as part of the multiomics dataset. Agreement on this observation.

Strong agreement on timing experiment (C11-C12, C85-C95, C118). Both support the finding that switching glucose after infection provides no benefit. OpenEval notes this demonstrates early metabolic state is critical. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges this 'very important' negative result and its clinical implications. High concordance.

Both support hIAIP supplementation findings (C13, C96-C104, C121). OpenEval notes the unexpected detrimental effect with plausible mechanistic explanation, appropriately calling it speculative. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge. Agreement on the data and its interpretation as an additional mechanistic insight.

Disagreement on bacterial burden correlation analysis (C51). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting within-group correlations suggest tolerance/adaptation rather than clearance as mechanism. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, finding the correlation analysis 'insufficient to fully resolve the relationship' and questioning whether omics changes could still be due to bacterial load. Peer review more skeptical of the interpretation.

OpenEval supports osmolality control experiment (C40-C41) as important for ruling out osmotic confounding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on this control.

OpenEval supports finding that glucose-driven metabolic reprogramming occurs independently of infection (C59). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address this dissection of mechanisms.
OpenEval supports baseline IL-10 finding (C50) but notes mechanism unexplored. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on this observation.

OpenEval supports normoglycemia achievement (C117) as important optimization. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges authors 'mitigate...hypoglycemia...by using a slightly high amount of glucose,' confirming this finding. Agreement that this represents clinical feasibility.

Both support integrative conclusions about hepatic metabolism (C112, C115-C116). OpenEval notes convergence of multiomics data supporting liver as key mediator, acknowledging inference limitations. Peer reviewers accept this interpretation as a novel insight without challenge. Agreement on this major mechanistic conclusion.

OpenEval rates speculative future directions (C120, C123-C124) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting these are untested hypotheses for follow-up. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address these speculative proposals.

OpenEval rates explanation for hIAIP effects (C122) as UNCERTAIN speculation requiring further investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted the hIAIP findings but did not specifically evaluate this mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval supports overarching conclusion (C125) about clinical translation potential while noting need for human trials. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as a discrete result, though the editor's summary affirms the study is 'supported by convincing data' and has translational relevance.

Partial overlap on gluconeogenesis gene expression (C55-C57). OpenEval supports the inference as well-supported by pathway-specific enzymes. Peer Reviewer 2 challenges this interpretation, showing the gene patterns may contradict the authors' claims. Disagreement on whether transcriptomic data support enhanced gluconeogenesis.

Partial overlap on metabolomic support for gluconeogenesis (C65-C66). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without direct flux measurement. Peer reviewers accept metabolomic data (C65-C66) without challenge as part of the multiomics dataset. Some divergence: OpenEval more cautious about mechanistic interpretation than peer acceptance of raw data suggests.
